newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Inter-Korean Red Cross talks set for Beijing.
newsitem.headline: Inter-Korean Red Cross talks set for Beijing.

text.p: South Korea's Red Cross said on Tuesday it had agreed on Beijing as the venue for a new round of talks with its Northern counterpart on speeding up food aid, and the meeting would be held on Friday.
It had proposed Seoul, Pyongyang or the border village of Panmunjom as the venue to reopen talks that stalled earlier this month. But Pyongyang insisted on the Chinese capital.
The president of the South Korean Red Cross, Kang Young-hoon, communicated his acceptance in a message relayed to the North over a telephone "hotline" at Panmunjom, a Red Cross statement said.
"I have decided to send delegates to Beijing with a view to solving the difficulties our brethren in North Korea are suffering as quickly as possible," his message said.
"I still do not understand the real intention behind your insistence on holding the meeting in Beijing, rather than in our our country, which would be more convenient. It is regrettable," he said.

The last round of talks on May 3 and 5 were also held in Beijing. But they broke down after the North, which is suffering from chronic food shortages, demanded to know the exact amount of aid it could expect before discussing moves to speed up delivery.
